reports.executiveSummary:
This week focused on reporting Sport Methodology Programme progress, supporting athletes and coaches preparing for the CAC and Commonwealth Games, and advancing federation development.

A report was delivered at the Dominica Olympic Committee AGM, outlining achievements, needs, and next steps across six areas: high-performance and institutional capacity; technical expertise and coach pathways; shared facilities and visibility; government–DOC cooperation; sport investment; and strategic planning and income diversification.

Athletes, coaches, and Chefs de Mission received support. Communication between regular and Games coaches was facilitated where possible.

objectives.objective: Provide additional, athlete-centred support to athletes, coaches, Chefs de Mission, and other members of the athlete entourage preparing for the CAC Games and Commonwealth Games.
objectives.expectedResult:
Through practical templates, planning tools, WhatsApp communication, Zoom sessions, in-person meetings, and ongoing coordination with the Chefs de Mission and athlete entourage, athletes and coaches will develop a clearer understanding that each athlete has different preparation, communication, and competition-support needs.
Athletes will have a structured way to communicate what they need before, during, and after competition. Coaches and other members of the athlete entourage will be better prepared to provide individualized support based on each athlete’s routines, preferences, and performance needs. This personalized approach is practical and achievable within the context of Dominica’s relatively small Games delegations.
objectives.successIndicator: A multisport Competition Centering Routine and Performance Support Plan is shared with athletes and coaches attending the CAC Games and Commonwealth Games. Coaches receive a practical tool to help them understand and support athletes with whom they may not regularly work. An online preparatory session is conducted with coaches attending the Games. A recording of the session is provided to coaches and delegation personnel who are unable to attend live. Athletes, or the coaches and support personnel who regularly work with them, communicate relevant information to the coaches attending the Games and, where appropriate, to the wider delegation. Information shared addresses what each athlete may need to think, feel, hear, and do at key moments before competition, between events, immediately after competition, and during the post-Games period. Communication is facilitated, where possible, between athletes’ regular coaches and the coaches who will support them at the Games. Additional individual check-ins are conducted with athletes to review their preparation, recent competitions, current concerns, and support needs. Athletes and coaches who need to discuss the support schedulefollow up meetings with the coaches attending the games, the Sport Methodologist and the local Affiliate Sport Methodology Officer

objectives.expectedResult: Basketball and Volleyball receive draft development pathways and workforce-management tools grounded in FIBA and FIVB best practices. Cycling is engaged through direct consultation with its leadership, coaches and athletes and is supported in identifying athlete needs and developing its pathway using relevant UCI and long-term development principles. The three federations are encouraged to review and adapt the resources developed by sport methodologists to Dominica’s context while identifying gaps in athlete development, coaching capacity, referee or official qualifications and certification opportunities.
objectives.successIndicator: The Sport Methodologist and Local Sport Methodology Officer developed structured draft athlete-development pathways for Basketball and Volleyball. The basketball pathway draws on FIBA best practices, the Jr. NBA curriculum and long-term athlete development principles. The volleyball pathway draws on FIVB best practices and established long-term athlete development principles. Both pathways define the technical, tactical, physical and personal competencies athletes should progressively develop from childhood through the youth, young adult and high-performance levels. A meeting was held with Cycling President Mr. Ronald Charles, Coach Levi Baron and athletes Kohath Baron, Stephan Carbon and Ross Semper to discuss athlete development, high-performance preparation and the recent training-camp experience in Trinidad and Tobago. The Cycling athletes had an opportunity to describe the skills acquired during the camp, their current training and competition priorities, and the equipment repairs and bicycle adjustments they require. Follow-up priorities were identified for Kohath Baron, including assessment of his recovery, equipment, training and other support needs following each competition weekend in Italy as he prepares for the Canadian Championships and World Championships. As less work had been completed on the cycling development levels, the Cycling Association was asked to provide the technical competencies athletes should develop at each stage. The Association was also asked to help define the progressive education and qualification requirements for cycling coaches and officials or commissaires. Coach and referee or official databases were developed or prepared for federation input to verify active personnel, qualifications, certification levels, current roles and development needs. The federations were asked to update their High-Performance Athlete Databases, National Federation Databases and Multi-Cycle Operations, Shared Calendars and Participation Plans. Research and external consultation were initiated regarding coach, referee and official-development opportunities available through FIBA Americas, the FIVB, the UCI and relevant regional bodies. The Volleyball Association reported that national-team training had resumed. Basketball and Volleyball were encouraged to schedule executive meetings to review and validate their draft pathways. Cycling was asked to review the documents in its shared federation folder and participate in a follow-up meeting after providing the required technical information. All three federations were encouraged to identify additional coaches for the available Panam Sports online coach-education programme. Follow-up communication was prepared for the federation presidents outlining the work completed, outstanding documents and next steps relating to performance, high performance, operations and integrity.

objectives.objective:
The primary strategic goal of the TTOC was to work with the Ministry of Sport to change the elite athlete funding model. This was supposed to be addressed during Phase 2 of the project, in which the top 40 TT athletes from three sports were identified and each given a Performance Gap analysis. Then, detailed LA28 athlete plans were collected from three different NGB/NSO's and a meeting was set to meet with the Ministry of Sport. Forty-eight hours before the meeting, the Minister canceled the meeting and has yet to reschedule.

On May 13, I submitted the Phase 3 proposal for consideration to the TTOC, which detailed the next steps for the LA28 plans and the 2036 Strategic Plan process. That proposal has yet to be approved and actioned.

Thus everything for the TTOC Project is on hold.
